lifecycles._note: COVERAGE-ONLY guarded lifecycle for the mariadb DBaaS cluster sub-op WRITE endpoints. It does NOT provision a real billable cluster: it soft-captures an EXISTING cluster_id (+ instance_group_id / bsg_id / log_type) from read-only list/show calls; when none exists the {{cluster_id}} (and {{instance_group_id}}/{{bsg_id}}/{{log_type}}/{{origin_cluster_id}}/{{replica_cluster_id}}) tokens still normalize to the catalog '*' key so each endpoint is CALLED and RECORDED (a 404/400/403/409/422 counts as covered per the engine). Every mutating step is optional+grouped+broad-expect_status so an isolated 4xx records coverage WITHOUT failing the run or chaining a real create->mutate->delete. heavy:true gates behind SCP_RUN_HEAVY; DELETEs are destructive:true. Bodies derive from the shared SCP DBaaS shape + per-endpoint api_docs request_example (data/api_bodies.json only has createcluster) and are UNPROVEN — promote to validated after a real 2xx. The relational engines (mysql/mariadb/epas/postgresql) share ONE body template; mariadb adds audit-log (PUT /audit-log).

lifecycles._note: COVERAGE-ONLY read lifecycle for mariadb id-bound GETs. Soft-captures an existing cluster_id (from /v1/clusters) and dbaas_engine_version_id (from /v1/engine-versions), then a probe_reads step exercises EVERY mariadb catalog GET whose path params are satisfied (replicas via cluster_id, engine-version properties via dbaas_engine_version_id, requests via a literal placeholder request_id) so each id-bound GET is CALLED and RECORDED under its own catalog key (a 4xx counts as covered). 100% read-only: every step optional + grouped, broad expect_status. requests/{request_id} is KNOWN-HARD: request_id is returned only by async ops and is not listable, so a literal placeholder id is used purely so the endpoint is reached (4xx expected).

HEAVY 2026-07-16 (svccov-mariadb session, owner-approved SCP_RUN_HEAVY): dedicated 1-cluster campaign for the version-axis + new-instance-ops gap keys that mariadb-cluster-subops-a/b (database__subops-full.json) can't reach on a single-major cluster: mariadbupgrademajorversion, mariadbpatchminorversion, mariadbshowinstance, mariadbmanualbackup, mariadbexportlog. Ported STRUCTURALLY from the live-proven mysql-cluster-version-upgrade (database__mysql.json, 2026-07-16 svccov-mysql session) with mariadb's OWN live-verified specifics. LIVE GET /v1/engine-versions 2026-07-16 (svccov-mariadb session): contents[0]=11.4.10 id fd5ca852145b498783de6dbd0762e146 (newest 11.4 minor), contents[1]=11.4.7 id 5828d309085e4094808614ce0694e8c6 (oldest 11.4 minor -- only 2 minors in the 11.4 major, unlike mysql's 3 in 8.4), contents[2]=10.11.15 id 1a83ff91141d419aafb26eae8986b2b9 (newest 10.11 minor), contents[3..5]=10.11.13/10.11.9/10.11.8 (older 10.11 minors) -- ASSUMES this descending-by-recency order holds; re-derive indices from a fresh GET if a run shows a capture mismatch. STRATEGY: create the cluster on the OLD MAJOR (10.11, via where_prefix match -> whichever 10.11 entry sorts first, here 10.11.15) -> mariadbupgrademajorversion jumps it to the OLDEST 11.4 minor (11.4.7, contents[1]) -> mariadbpatchminorversion then jumps 11.4.7 -> 11.4.10 (newest, contents[0]) on the SAME cluster, mirroring mysql's proven single-cluster version-axis chain. MinorPatchRequest body: {backup_before_upgrade: bool REQUIRED, software_version: string REQUIRED} per mysql precedent (data/api_docs.json model requires backup_before_upgrade even though some doc examples omit it) -- verify live on this run; if mariadb's model differs the actual response will show it. PatchRequest (major-version-upgrade) body: {dbaas_engine, software_version} -- dbaas_engine is captured LIVE from the cluster's own detail GET ($.dbaas_engine), never hardcoded (mysql's case-sensitivity quirk 'MySQL' vs 'mysql' means mariadb's own casing must be captured, not assumed). mariadbshowinstance needs path param instance_name (a NAME not an id) captured from $.instance_groups[0].instances[0].name. mariadbmanualbackup takes NO request body per the docs model (path cluster_id only), mirrors mysqlmanualbackup. mariadbexportlog log_type is a fixed enum (alert|audit|slow, data/api_docs.json database/mariadb/mariadbexportlog) -- tries all 3 values sequentially (own group each) since mysql only proved 'alert' works and the owner asked us to also try 'audit' for mariadb specifically; registration is PF-blocked per orchestrator brief (500 ContactAdminForAssistance class) so export is attempted WITHOUT a registered config, same as mysql. mariadbremovebackuphistories: body key IS ALREADY 'backup_history_number' (verified correct in this file's mariadb-cluster-subops-guarded AND database__subops-full.json's mariadb-cluster-subops-a -- no typo present, contrary to the orchestrator brief's assumption); its prior 401 Dbaas.Unauthorized.AuthNFailed (knowledge/validated-facts.md 2026-06-10, reconfirmed HB1 2026-07-04) is a known backend auth quirk shared across mysql/mariadb/postgresql/epas/cachestore, NOT a body-shape bug -- reconfirmed once more here for the record, not re-litigated. C-group (mariadbcreaterestore, mariadbcreateotherregionreplica, mariadbswitchovercluster) deliberately EXCLUDED -- each needs its own extra billable cluster or ha_enabled=true, out of this session's single-cluster/time budget; left as a follow-up lever. Steps carry their own create-vpc(10.144.0.0/20)/create-subnet(10.144.3.0/24) + adopt:'vpc'/'subnet#db' markers mirroring the mysql template, but LIVE-OBSERVED 2026-07-16 (svccov-mariadb session, 2 aborted attempts, both properly torn down -- see below) this lifecycle IS registered in dependencies.json adopt_edges (needed for validate_dag's 0-gap check), and shared_infra.shared_needs() keys off the STEP-LEVEL adopt marker, not the DAG registration: it always provisions a fresh SESSION-SCOPED shared VPC/subnet (10.124.0.0/20 pool) and this lifecycle's own create-vpc/create-subnet steps get SKIPPED ('adopting shared vpc=... (skip create)') -- the 10.144.0.0/20 CIDR above is therefore never actually used at runtime; this matches mysql-cluster-version-upgrade's identical mechanism (its 'own dedicated VPC' framing is equally inaccurate for the same structural reason). Not a functional problem (the shared VPC/subnet is torn down at pytest session end same as a self-created one would be) but the code MUST run to full pytest-session completion for that teardown fixture to fire. OPERATIONAL LESSON (2026-07-16, cost this session both of its live-run budget before reaching cluster-create): invoke via run_in_background:true (or nohup+disown) -- a foreground shell call that hits the harness's own ~2min default timeout gets SIGKILLed WITHOUT running pytest's session teardown, orphaning the shared VPC+subnet (2 such orphans this session, both manually recovered via their reports/registry/<APITEST_RUN_ID>.jsonl records -- subnets then vpc, confirmed 404 -- do NOT use a raw account-wide list+delete for this, use the run's own registry file). NEXT ATTEMPT: SCP_CRUD_IDS=mariadb-cluster-version-upgrade SCP_RUN_HEAVY=true APITEST_RUN_ID=svccov-mariadb-<epoch> python -m pytest tests/crud -m crud -x -q backgrounded from the start; expect create+major-upgrade+minor-patch+manual-backup+delete to take on the order of an hour given each step's generous settle timeouts (2400s create wait, 3600s post-major-upgrade wait, 1800s post-patch wait) -- budget the FULL session runway for one attempt, do not split into a second short probe.
